sources.entry: Squidex - Headless CMS, based on MongoDB, CQRS and Event Sourcing. (Demo, Source Code) MIT .NET

summary.one_liner: Squidex is an open source headless CMS and content management hub built with ASP.NET Core and CQRS, exposing a rich API with OData filters and Swagger definitions.
summary.what_it_does: Squidex provides content management as a headless backend: rather than shipping a website UI, it offers an API with OData filter support and Swagger definitions so you can build your own front end, native app, or another server on top of it. The README says it is built with ASP.NET Core and CQRS and tested on Windows and Linux with modern browsers. Development prerequisites listed are Visual Studio Code or Visual Studio 2022, Node.js (development only), MongoDB, PostgreSQL, MySQL or SQL Server, and the .NET 8 SDK. Deployment documentation is linked for Azure, AWS, Docker, GCP, Heroku, IIS, Kubernetes, Render, and Vultr. The README also mentions that a SaaS cloud version is available. Community contributors are credited with features such as Google Maps support, FTP and GridFS asset stores, Azure Store support, and a Kafka rule action.
use_cases: headless content management for websites and apps
managing content through a REST/OData API
serving content to native mobile or desktop apps
self-hosted content hub with custom front ends
storing assets in FTP, GridFS, or Azure stores
how_to_run: Install the .NET 8 SDK and Visual Studio Code or Visual Studio 2022
Provision MongoDB, PostgreSQL, MySQL, or SQL Server
Clone the repository and build the project
Follow the deployment docs for Docker, Kubernetes, IIS, or a cloud platform
notable: Headless design with OData filtering and Swagger/OpenAPI definitions
Multiple database backends: MongoDB, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server
Built on ASP.NET Core with CQRS architecture
Asset store options contributed by the community, including FTP, GridFS, and Azure
Documented deployment paths for Docker, Kubernetes, IIS, and several clouds
caveats: Docs are described in the README as a work in progress
Requires a separate database server (MongoDB, PostgreSQL, MySQL, or SQL Server) and the .NET 8 SDK for building
Feature requests and help go through a community forum rather than the README itself
